qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Sole-source builder of US Navy nuclear aircraft carriers (Newport News) and major surface combatants (Ingalls) possesses unreplicable physical drydock infrastructure. However, as a dedicated defense contractor serving a monopsonist customer (US Navy represents ~85% of revenue), allowable margins are capped under Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR). 5-year median GAAP ROIC of ~6-8% (10-year median 9.8%) and operating margins of 5-7% fail the 12% ROIC hurdle. Fixed-price incentive contracts expose HII to acute wage inflation and skilled trade shortages without commercial pricing power.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% & Lack of Commercial Pricing Power, REJECT). While HII controls irreplaceable nuclear shipyard infrastructure, defense monopsony contracting caps returns on invested capital well below the 12% threshold (5Y median GAAP ROIC ~6-8%, 10Y median 9.8%). High capital intensity and exposure to fixed-price cost overruns from skilled labor shortages prevent world-class compounding.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC of 9.8% with 2021-2025 ROIC averaging 5-8% (2021: 5.8%, 2022: 6.0%, 2023: 8.0%, 2024: 4.8%, 2025: 5.9%). Operating margins remain compressed in the 5.0%-7.5% range due to fixed-price incentive contract cost absorption amid severe skilled blue-collar labor shortages (certified nuclear welders and pipefitters). 2024 FCF collapsed to ~$40M before rebounding to $800M in 2025. Long-term debt stands at ~$2.5B-$2.8B against ~$550M-$650M normalized net income. The monopsonistic procurement structure of the US Navy legally caps contractor margins, structurally precluding economic returns above the cost of capital.
